article.title: The Shutter & Stairs Journal
article.description: Shobha Hegde's second-income search across Uttarahalli, Kathriguppe and the Kengeri arc — buying corner sites and small rented buildings where a shop's rent pays for the house above it.
article.quote: "Rent from the shop pays for the house above it."

tabs.name: Profile
tabs.label: Profile
tabs.title: Who they are
tabs.description: Getting to know Shobha Hegde (48, school administrator) — deploying ₹95L savings and ₹85L loan capacity into a shop-over-flat corner building that outlives her salary.

buyers.name: Shobha Hegde
buyers.description: Grew up watching her grandmother in Shivamogga collect rent from two shops attached to the family house — small money that arrived every month, every monsoon. That model imprinted on her. Walks the commercial cross-roads of Banashankari and Kathriguppe on Sunday mornings, counting shutters and noting which bakeries survive.
buyers.imagegenerationprompt: A stylized vector graphic portrait illustration of a 48-year-old South Indian woman school administrator named Shobha with neat pulled-back black hair streaked with grey, wearing a plain cotton kurti, digital vector art style with fine dark outlines, posterized cel-shading, warm natural skin tones, warm determined smiling expression, clean solid warm beige background (#F4EBE1), high quality character art.

tabs.sharedVisionDescription: Buy a corner site or small rented building where a pharmacy or condiments shop pays ~₹60,000 downstairs, two 1BHKs pay ₹24,000 each upstairs, and their old age becomes a ledger of rent receipts rather than a request to their daughter.

quotes.text: Good handwriting hiding bad paper — the neat ledger was the trap, alva.
quotes.author: — Shobha

quotes.text: The ledger was real, madam. The problem was underneath it.
quotes.author: — Riya

quotes.text: If you ever needed the shop back… you'd be in court, not in business.
quotes.author: — Riya

quotes.text: My bhajan group is worth more than your database.
quotes.author: — Shobha

chatMessages.text: Riya, nija helbeku — I liked that building too much. Rent ledger was so neat, ree. Forty years of entries. My grandmother would have cried seeing it.

The ledger was real, madam. The problem was underneath — the tenancy predates every agreement on file. Now, this time, you talk to the pharmacy chain before we bid. An LOI from a tenant changes your whole negotiation.

tabs.insightTitle: What I noticed while we were searching
tabs.insightDescription: “Shobha counted footfall herself — Tuesday 11 am, then Sunday 6 pm — before she'd take a single broker call. She wasn't projecting her grandmother's Shivamogga street onto Bengaluru; she was insisting the street prove itself. The bounce taught her the rest: a rent ledger is only as good as the tenancy paperwork beneath it.”

tabs.rejectedTitle: How the corner-scarcity loop stalls the hunt

rejectedReasons.title: Guaranteed-Tenant Detour
rejectedReasons.count: bank never heard of the plan

tabs.suggestionDescription: Stay on corners where you have personally counted footfall, source the tenant LOI yourself — your bajan-group network is worth more than a broker's database — and buy a smaller proven corner over a bigger speculative one. A managed asset would be kinder to future-Shobha, but it wouldn't be hers.

tabs.name: Learnings
tabs.label: Learnings
tabs.title: What this journey teaches us.
tabs.description: Key takeaways for rental-income builders buying small corners and rented buildings for a second income.

lessons.title: The corner premium is brutally efficient.
lessons.description: Every location that guarantees a pharmacy tenant costs exactly what the pharmacy's rent justifies. The market has already done her math; her edge must be patience, not discovery.
lessons.imagegenerationprompt: A 3D vector illustration of a corner premium priced exactly in line with a pharmacy's justified rent, rendered in an 80% greyscale monochrome palette (#1E1E1E to #FFFFFF) with Warm Coral #FF8A65 price accents, Scandinavian minimalism, clean white background.

lessons.title: A rent ledger is only as good as its paperwork.
lessons.description: Sitting tenants are an asset and a legal fact — read the tenancy agreements and rent-control history before falling in love with a ledger.
lessons.imagegenerationprompt: A 3D vector illustration of an aged rent ledger with a magnifying glass over the tenancy agreement beneath it, rendered in an 80% greyscale monochrome palette (#1E1E1E to #FFFFFF) with a Warm Coral #FF8A65 magnifier accent, Scandinavian minimalism, clean white background.

lessons.title: A locked contractor rate is the only budget.
lessons.description: Construction quotes moved 12% in six months. A build plan without a locked rate is a wish, not a budget — favour buy-built when quotes inflate.
lessons.imagegenerationprompt: A 3D vector illustration of two construction quotes six months apart with the 12% jump bracketed, rendered in an 80% greyscale monochrome palette (#1E1E1E to #FFFFFF) with a Warm Coral #FF8A65 bracket accent, Scandinavian minimalism, clean white background.

lessons.title: Your radius rule is often wiser than you are.
lessons.description: The 20-minute scooter rule eliminated a 'perfect' Kengeri deal — and a week later, Shobha knew the rule had been the wiser of the two of them.
lessons.imagegenerationprompt: A 3D vector illustration of a scooter-mapped radius circle around a south Bengaluru home with a corner pin outside it, rendered in an 80% greyscale monochrome palette (#1E1E1E to #FFFFFF) with a Warm Coral #FF8A65 radius ring accent, Scandinavian minimalism, clean white background.

beforeItems.text: A shop-corner that looks busy is busy
A neat rent ledger means a safe building
Building ourselves saves the most money
Any promising corner near home will do

afterItems.text: Footfall is counted twice-weekly, in person, per corner
Tenancy paperwork behind the ledger is the real asset
Buy-built with visible rent receipts often beats building
The radius rule usually knows better than the buyer

chatMessages.text: Hakki mele, Riya — the neat ledger was the trap. Good handwriting hiding bad paper. My grandmother's model was right; I just needed paper to back the receipts.
And that is exactly how a second income is built, madam — one shutter with a signed LOI, one corner with counted footfall, at a time.

tabs.adviceDescription: For families building a second income from shop-over-flat property, the thriftiest path is counted footfall, paper-backed ledgers, tenant LOIs sourced personally, and banks known before offers. Shobha proved that patience is the strategy — and that a covered radius rule usually knows more than the buyer.
